PullRequest.Title: Fix browser double-navigating pages opened via `window.open`

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Every allowed window.open popup previously combined Chromium's navigation of the returned WebContents with a second explicit WebContents.loadURL of the same URL, repeating page fetch, document parsing, lifecycle events, and associated subresource work once per popup.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Pages opened through window.open were navigated twice, causing duplicate network/page-load work and added popup-open latency; for about:blank popups subsequently populated with document.write, the extra load also replaced the initial document.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: Popup WebContents supplied by Electron no longer receive an additional explicit loadURL; Chromium completes the original window.open navigation once. Child views without supplied WebContents still receive their initial URL through the existing loadURL path.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: In the base revision, BrowserView.setWindowOpenHandler passes Electron's existing popup WebContents and details.url into _createChildView (browserView.ts:187-226). The callback at browserViewMainService.ts:431-439 always copied that URL to initialUrl, and _createBrowserView then unconditionally invoked view.loadURL(initialUrl) at lines 477-481. Electron also completes the original window.open navigation after createWindow returns the same WebContents, so the base path issued a second navigation for each allowed popup. The changed line gates initialUrl when electronOptions.webContents exists, while preserving explicit loading for child views created without existing WebContents (browserView.ts:769).

Scenarios.Scenario: A listed integrated-browser page opens a URL popup via target=_blank or window.open(url).
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The opener's setWindowOpenHandler synchronously creates the child BrowserView and returns its supplied WebContents; Chromium then completes the popup navigation. The diff removes the additional asynchronous loadURL from this path, so only Chromium's navigation must complete before the popup page is usable.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Navigate the popup WebContents and fetch/parse the target page and its subresources.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One navigation per allowed URL popup after the diff; before the diff Chromium navigated the returned WebContents and the service also called loadURL once, producing two navigation attempts per popup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The base revision always propagated details.url as initialUrl even when Electron supplied WebContents, causing one additional loadURL per popup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The remaining Chromium navigation is required for popup readiness; the removed explicit navigation duplicated network and document-load work and could extend or restart the critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Emit the serialized browser-view created event toward the owning window.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One created event per popup before and after the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same one created event was emitted per popup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Not increased by the diff; it announces the child editor while navigation proceeds.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Apply Electron session proxy settings when the child acquires a changed remote proxy.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one setProxy for a changed proxy configuration; same-proxy acquisitions are coalesced by sameProxyInfo, and local/global sessions do not start a remote proxy.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical acquire/setProxy behavior, followed by a duplicate explicit navigation that waited for proxy readiness.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The Chromium-owned popup navigation did not await whenReady before the diff and still does not; only the removed explicit loadURL awaited it, so the diff does not add or move this boundary onto the path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of allowed popups, with effective navigation cardinality reduced from up to two per popup to one; page/subresource size determines the saved network, CPU, and rendering work.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One Chromium navigation per popup after the change. Different popups remain independent and unbounded by a shared limiter, but the prior same-popup pair of Chromium navigation plus explicit loadURL is reduced from up to 2N navigations to N for N popups.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: On a cold HTTP cache the removed load could duplicate page and subresource transfers. On a warm cache bytes may be served locally, but the second navigation, document parsing, lifecycle events, and rendering work still occurred. There is no application cache or negative-cache behavior on this creation path.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the supplied WebContents and URL flow into initialUrl, which directly triggers loadURL in addition to Electron completing window.open on the returned WebContents.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Popup frequency and page/subresource size vary, and HTTP caching may reduce duplicate transferred bytes, but duplicate navigation in the base path and its removal are directly established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression introduced. The change removes repeated network/page-load work; the concrete regression fix was recorded against its introducing commit.

Scenarios.Scenario: A page opens about:blank and synchronously populates the child with document.write, as covered by the added smoke case.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: window.open must synchronously receive the returned child WebContents, then document.write/document.close constructs the initial document. With supplied WebContents, the diff avoids scheduling a second about:blank load that would replace or rebuild that document.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create a WebContentsView around Electron's popup WebContents and initialize its about:blank document.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One child WebContents and one initial document per popup after the change; the base path additionally invoked loadURL('about:blank') once per popup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The service explicitly loaded about:blank after wrapping the WebContents, duplicating Chromium-owned initial-document navigation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Child creation and document.write are required; the removed load no longer races with or repeats initial-document setup.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send the created browser-view event for the child editor.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required for the workbench tab to appear; unchanged by the conditional initialUrl.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of script-created blank popups; redundant initialization decreases by one per popup.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One in-process initial-document construction per popup. Multiple popups can be created independently; the diff removes one redundant load per popup rather than adding concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: about:blank has no remote cache lookup, application cache, or negative-cache behavior. The relevant saved work is in-process navigation/document reconstruction.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added test exercises supplied popup WebContents with an empty URL, and the changed condition is exactly the branch that suppresses the old explicit about:blank load.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The CPU savings per blank popup are small and popup frequency varies; the mechanism is certain, while the main value is preventing replacement of the authored initial document.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression; this path performs less navigation and allocation work than before.

Scenarios.Scenario: A child view is created without Electron-supplied WebContents, including pinned-navigation redirection to a new integrated-browser child.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The child callback receives electronOptions undefined, so the changed conditional preserves initialUrl. _createBrowserView still waits for any remote proxy via BrowserView.loadURL before the single explicit navigation completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch and render the redirected child URL.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One network navigation per child before and after the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The URL was assigned to initialUrl and loaded once; the conditional still does so because no existing WebContents is supplied.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The navigation and remote-proxy readiness remain on the child-open critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Apply changed tunnel-proxy settings to the Electron session before explicit loadURL proceeds.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one setProxy for an actual proxy change, coalesced for same-proxy acquisitions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical proxy acquisition and readiness wait.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: BrowserView.loadURL awaits whenReady both before and after this PR.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of pinned-navigation child creations; effective boundary count remains one navigation per child.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One explicit navigation per child, unchanged. Separate child creations can navigate concurrently; this PR neither adds fan-out nor changes the limiter model.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Standard Electron/HTTP cold and warm cache behavior is unchanged. Same-proxy configuration is coalesced, while navigation responses follow normal browser cache policy.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the only new predicate is false when electronOptions.webContents is absent, preserving the exact prior initialUrl and loadURL flow.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual URL sizes and child-open frequency vary, but there is no changed work or boundary count on this branch.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance change and no finding.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed both changed files and all diff pages. The production conditional removes a duplicate popup navigation and does not add work to the supplied-WebContents, document.write, or ordinary child-navigation paths. No diff-introduced performance finding was found; one concrete repeated-work regression fix was recorded via blame.
